ground_truth: You know, is this America? I mean, the opposition party punted, everybody punted, and then it came to the people. background.speaker: [target]
background.text: Yes, I mean, undoubtedly. I mean, I've been talking about a whole, you know, laundry list of democratic reforms and structural changes that we should try to push. And, you know, we'll have to see what plausibly can be done in, you know, an eight week period.

background.speaker: SPEAKER_05
background.text: Is there one thing you want to do in particular?

ground_truth: I mean, there are things that I'm trying to push both legislatively and push with the administration. I mean, legislatively, I've got bipartisan legislation called the Press Act, which is to protect reporters against compulsory process of their notes and having to produce their notes by subpoena. So it's basically to reinforce the freedom of the press so that reporters and the media are not going to be tyrannized during this period. It's bipartisan legislation I have with a colleague named Kevin Kiley, and we want to try to get it through the Senate before this is all over. I mean, it's very practical, but it could be really meaningful if we go into a tough period. I mean, you go back to the Alien and Sedition Acts in 1798. That was an attack on immigrants. It was an attack on the political opposition. And it was an attack on the press, all of them together. So we've got to do whatever we can to insulate people.
